chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I said, 'For the woman who has been thrice divorced, is there for her dwelling (sukna) or expenses (nafaqah)?' He said, 'Is she pregnant?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'There is neither a dwelling for her nor expenses.'

key_terms.الْمُطَلَّقَةُ ثَلَاثاً: The woman who has been thrice divorced

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a thrice-divorced woman regarding housing and maintenance if she is not pregnant?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a woman who has received a triple divorce (thalath) is entitled to neither housing (sukna) nor financial maintenance (nafaqah) during her waiting period (iddah), provided she is not pregnant. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the triple divorcee in Shia jurisprudence, where the completion of the iddah finalizes the irrevocable separation, thereby terminating the husband's ongoing financial obligations. The dialogue with Sama'ah underscores the precision with which the Imams distinguished between the conditions of pregnancy and non-pregnancy in determining these rights.
